This has been one of my favorite purchases as of late. I had been using the paper filters until this went on sale, and this was a considerable upgrade. The paper filters would often allow spoonfuls of grounds through, which translates to many mouthfuls of grounds. This mesh filter does a much better job of keeping the grounds out while being reusable and maintaining the great flavor I've come to expect from the Aeropress. If you have an Aeropress and don't already own one of these, I would highly recommend rectifying that immediately :)
almost as good as the paper filter, and much better than any other mesh filter of any kind that i've tried

I use my aeropess every day and I was previously using paper filters. This mesh filter has been an excellent replacement. It is easy to wash, very fine holes, and less wasteful. I don't have any regrets about switching from paper filters to this mesh one.

Works great, is easy to clean (even after leaving it sit for a weekend, cleaning the grounds off was not trouble), and my coffee doesn't have any more sediment than with the paper filters.

One thing to be aware of - I have a Kyocera hand-crank ceramic burr grinder, and to work properly with this filter I had to move the grind two notches up (coarser) from the finest setting. Though Aeropress recommends the finest grind, with this filter it did clog entirely. Setting the grind slightly coarser solved it, and the coffee still comes out perfectly.
Used in my aero press. It is easy to clean, durable so far (20 uses) and it makes great coffee.
Great product.

Works great, easy to clean, allows the full flavor to press through.  I use this predominantly for the "inverted brew" approach -- making individual cups of coffee (not cappuccinos).  Haven't used one of the disposable filters since I got this.  I'm surprised AeroPress doesn't include one of these as a standard accessory -- seems like it would be far more environmentally conscious.
Perfect! Just what I was hoping. Very happy....no more paper filters!

I mainly picked this up because I ran out of paper and it was a cheaper alternative to other products on the market, and it had the fine mesh size I wanted.
To be honest, I can't taste much of a difference between this and paper other than a super fine silt that adds some body to the bottom of the cup. The orientation doesn't seem to matter, but I found the puck releases a lot easier from the side without the branding.

My biggest problem with the mesh-filter it that it allows too much 'mud' through, especially if you use anything below a coarse grind.  It also allows the water to flow through too easily during the brew process. A better option, IMO, is to use the metal disk filters which only drip a little while brewing, and they allow just the right amount of mud through.  The disks are also much more resilient and very easy to clean without worry about damage.
Unfortunately, the mesh left a residue at the bottom of my mug. The paper filters never do. Therefore, I went back to using them, and not the mesh.

I waited for at least a week to leave a review to ensure that product worked and did as described. And yes with a high five! It actually improved the flavor of my dark brew and removed the bitterness. A shout out to the company's customer care, too.

The coffee doesn't have enough time to brew properly and the fast flow makes it easy to misjudge the amount of water you're pouring in, causing the dreaded overflow mess. I tried prepping the grounds by wetting them first, which helps a *little* but not enough to make this filter appealing. Just ordered 700 paper filters, this one goes into the drawer.

I just started using the AeroPress recently but I've heard about it since a couple years back. I knew that once I had gotten hold of my Aeropress the first accessory that I needed to get was a re-useable filter as a long term investment being a heavy coffee drinker. There are many variants out there but I eventually settled for this based on the overall reviews and price point. I'll start off with the con which isn't too big a deal.
Cons:
I received the item in a pretty firm cardboard meant to protect the mesh, however I did notice that my mesh was a little bent in the middle. I hope and suspect that it did not affect the functionality that much. However, to constantly see a line (bent) on the mesh can be irritating at times. After the couple of uses, the bent has not enlarged in anyway but I just hoped that it would have arrived in a almost perfect condition for a new product.

Pros:
I must say that although there were a reviews about the bad fitment and thickness the one I received fitted very nicely into my aeropress without difficulty. The water did flow through rather fast but I suspect it was also in part due to the way the water is poured into the press (Should not be poured directly but rather use a spoon to shield the direct flow) This allowed the water to stay long enough in the press for me to fit the plunger in. Washing was a breeze with the mesh though I would recommend it to be handwashed instead of using a sponge as the lint would catch
The only problem is the mesh dont feet well

It is true that the water runs too quickly through the mesh, as other reviewers have said. I bought the filter because I was into cold brew and used the aeropress to filter out the grounds after it had steeped. I had to make two pours of the steeped coffee and disassemble and clean the press between pours or it clogged and splurted coffee everywhere. I thought a filter like this would work better for that purpose, but it doesn't. Also, I was drinking more decaf and wanted a clear way to distinguish between filters used for decaf and those used for regular espresso.
All that said, once I figured out how to make hot coffee using this filter it is so spectacular that I have not yet returned to cold brew! My secret: I tilt the press as it sits in my coffee cup, measure the water using the plunger and have the stirrer in my hand as I add the water. Tilting the Aeropress lets the grounds steep long enough, even though it is only maybe ten to twenty second longer. The flavor is full-bodied, winey and so rich that, for the first time in my life, I stopped adding cream because it detracted from the outstanding espresso experience. I love that the filter is so easy to clean (I use a dish brush to get under the edge of the rim). Much better coffee than with the paper filter. Can't compare to the other Altura filters because this is the only one I've tried. It seems to be very well-made and I am hoping to get years of use from it.
